problem_statement: The shell should support command aliases: a user-defined short token expands to a longer command before execution (for example, an alias 'stacks' expands to 'kernel thread stacks'), with a built-in '?' alias expanding to 'help'. Aliases defined in a host file should be compiled into the shell, tab-completion at the root level should offer matching alias names and complete them, alias subcommands should be tab-completed, an 'aliases' command should list the configured aliases, and an alias whose name collides with an existing root command in the current context (including a selected command subtree) must be ignored in favour of the real command rather than shadowing it.

verification.reason: The statement describes the alias feature conceptually but omits the Kconfig option names (CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES, CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES_FILE, CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES_HAS_FILE), the CMake function name (generate_shell_aliases_inc_file_for_target), and the exact collision warning text that the hidden tests require. All are public interface or observable behaviour that can be added to the statement without dictating the implementation.

problems.detail: The Kconfig option CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES is not named in the statement, but the hidden tests guard all alias tests with IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES) and the testcase.yaml sets CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES=y.

The Kconfig option CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES_FILE is not named in the statement, but the testcase.yaml sets CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES_FILE="shell_aliases.txt" and the test CMakeLists.txt reads it via ${CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES_FILE}.
The Kconfig option CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES_HAS_FILE is not named in the statement, but the test CMakeLists.txt uses if(CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES_HAS_FILE) and the test guards use it.

The CMake function generate_shell_aliases_inc_file_for_target is not named in the statement, but the test CMakeLists.txt calls it with (app, source, generated-path) arguments; without it the test target will not build.

The exact warning string 'Alias '<name>' ignored because command exists in current context' is checked by the collision tests via strstr, but the statement only says the alias 'must be ignored in favour of the real command rather than shadowing it' without specifying the message format.

leak_check.missing: Does not explicitly specify the aliases file syntax or the exact tab-completion behaviours exercised by the hidden tests, such as single-candidate completion inserting a trailing space and multiple-candidate printing/partial completion.

problem_statement_fixed: The shell should support command aliases, controlled by the Kconfig option CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES: a user-defined short token expands to a longer command before execution (for example, an alias 'stacks' expands to 'kernel thread stacks'), with a built-in '?' alias expanding to 'help'. Aliases defined in a host file, configured via the Kconfig option CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES_FILE (a string specifying the host-side file path) and detected by the Kconfig option CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES_HAS_FILE (a boolean that is true when CONFIG_SHELL_ALIASES_FILE is non-empty), should be compiled into the shell using the CMake function generate_shell_aliases_inc_file_for_target, which takes a target, a source file path, and a generated include file path. Tab-completion at the root level should offer matching alias names and complete them, alias subcommands should be tab-completed, an 'aliases' command should list the configured aliases, and an alias whose name collides with an existing root command in the current context (including a selected command subtree) must be ignored in favour of the real command rather than shadowing it. When such a collision is detected, the shell must print a warning message containing the text 'Alias '<name>' ignored because command exists in current context' where <name> is the alias name that collided.
